references.title: Laurence BonJour, Externalist Theories of Empirical Knowledge (1980), university-hosted PDF text
references.support: BonJour's Case IV (pp. 62–67) gives Norman's stipulated reliable clairvoyance, lack of evidence, and BonJour's objection from Norman's own epistemic perspective. Relevant passages were read in the PDF text extraction; the whole article was not read.

references.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Reliabilist Epistemology
references.support: Sections 2.1 and 4.2 discuss the clairvoyance challenge, distinct reliabilist responses, and evidentialist–reliabilist hybrids. Scholarly reference context; it does not establish that every reliabilist theory has the same verdict.

references.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Internalist vs. Externalist Conceptions of Epistemic Justification
references.support: Sections 1 and 2.1 distinguish debates about justification and knowledge, present BonJour's argument, and explain why the case does not by itself undermine every externalist view. Scholarly reference context, not a claim of consensus.

references.title: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Reliabilism
references.support: Section 3(a) reviews the objection that reliable true belief may be insufficient for justification, several replies, and Mr. Truetemp as a related but distinct case. Relevant passages were read; this is a reference-work synthesis, not primary testimony.

references.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, The Analysis of Knowledge
references.support: Section 3 explains the standard characterization of Gettier cases as justified true beliefs that nevertheless appear not to be knowledge because of epistemic luck; context for the article's qualified contrast with Norman.
